full_judgment:
Abdur Rahman Chowdhury, J.—This miscellaneous appeal and the two civil revision cases have been taken up together for hearing on the prayer of the parties since they arise out of the same suit and are directed against the same order. 

 3. The plaintiff also filed a Miscellaneous Appeal being F.M.A. No. 83/81 against the order passed by the trial Court rejecting the plaintiff's prayer for temporary injunction against the defendants for restraining them from making any pucca construction in the suit land and also changing the nature and character of the same. We have heard the learned Counsels of both the parties at length, perused the impugned order, the petitions and the affidavits on record. 

 6. Since the question of injunction involved in the Misc. Appeal is dependent upon the decision with regard to the question of maintainability of the suit itself, we first propose to take up the question of maintainability. The records of the case are not called for but the parties produced the certified copies of relevant papers necessary for the disposal of the matter under consideration. 

 11. Now a comparative perusal of the reliefs claimed in both the suits, as stated above, would show that the reliefs prayed for in paragraph 17(b) of the present suit are substantially the same as in paragraph (1) of the earlier suit, inasmuch as, in both the prayers the plaintiffs had asked for a direction upon the defendants 2-4 to execute the deed of transfer in favour of the plaintiffs in respect of their share in the property. In prayer (b) the plaintiffs had also prayed for a decree declaring the defendants 2-4 as trustees in respect of the Schedule-A land for the beneficial interest of the plaintiffs. This admittedly was nowhere the case of the plaintiff in the earlier suit. 

 Now coming to the Miscellaneous Appeal which arose out of the rejection of the plaintiffs prayer for temporary injunction, no decision is called for in view of our decision to dismiss the suit. 

 15. In the result, therefore, the Rule in Civil Revision No. 22/81 is made absolute and the Rule in Civil Revision No. 72/81 is also accordingly dismissed and the ad-interim order of status quo passed by this court is also hereby vacated. In the facts and circumstances of the case, there will, however, be no order as to costs.
